prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1458; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for side impact collision at signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle entered on a red signal and struck the driver's side. Airbags did not deploy. Vehicles towed from scene. Police report requested from responding agency.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's counsel, who confirmed representation and requested that all further contact be routed through their office. Counsel indicated client was transported by ambulance and is complaining of neck and back strain. Medical records requested with signed authorization. Reserve set for bodily injury and property damage pending review.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photographs and preliminary police narrative. Damage pattern is consistent with a side impact at right angle. Witness statement obtained from pedestrian at corner indicating the opposing vehicle did not stop at the limit line. Liability leaning toward the other driver, subject to signal timing data from the municipality.

Entry 4: Received treatment summary from claimant's medical provider noting cervical and lumbar strain, with physical therapy recommended. Counsel submitted a demand package and requested an independent medical exam be scheduled before any settlement discussion. IME request sent to vendor and claimant's counsel notified.

Entry 5: Adverse carrier accepted liability in principle and agreed to contribute to the bodily injury claim. Negotiations with counsel ongoing regarding medical specials and wage loss documentation. Property damage appraisal completed on insured vehicle and total loss determination is under review. File remains open and flagged for supervisor review.
